source_review.notes: Checked NIST's current publication records for SP 800-145, SP 500-292 and SP 800-146; ISO's current records for ISO/IEC 22123-1:2023, 22123-2:2023 and 22123-3:2023; the ISO/IEC TS 25052-1 cloud quality record; and ENISA's 2023 cloud market analysis. The chapter identifies withdrawn ISO/IEC 17788/17789 lineage, preserves NIST's exact five/three/four baseline, and labels multi-cloud and serverless without promoting them to universal replacement categories.

evidence: Checked characteristic set C, service set S, deployment set D, exact contract K, classification function f(o,r), and consumer/provider control sets L_c and L_p.
Checked Cartesian-product notation S x D and the role-relative classification qualifier.
Checked service, deployment, tenancy, portability, interoperability and exit terms against NIST/ISO reference records.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Set notation is a teaching abstraction and does not imply that every real offering has one unambiguous pair.

evidence: Confirmed three encoded service models and four encoded deployment models.
Confirmed Cartesian-product count 3 x 4 equals 12.
Confirmed illustrative consumer-managed software layers count as two for IaaS, one for PaaS and zero for SaaS.
Confirmed all six stdout lines exactly match the snippet annotation and generated report.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Layer counts simplify one software-control view and are not a complete shared-responsibility matrix.

evidence: Checked independence argument: offered capability/control boundary and eligible infrastructure community answer different questions.
Checked role-relative classification where a SaaS provider can consume underlying PaaS/IaaS while its customer consumes SaaS.
Checked hybrid definition requires unique constituent clouds plus binding for data/application portability.
Checked that multi-provider inventory does not logically entail hybrid integration, portability or resilience.
Checked service labels cannot derive exact tenancy, location, service level, security, economics or exit terms without contract K.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The taxonomy supports disciplined comparison; it is not a formal proof of service properties.

evidence: Reviewed hosted non-cloud virtualization, private/community/public/hybrid clouds, unrelated multi-provider services and integrated multi-cloud cases.
Reviewed IaaS, application PaaS, managed database, managed Kubernetes, functions/serverless, hosted software and composed provider relationships.
Reviewed quota/capacity, disconnected use, provider/control-plane outage, tenancy, identity, location, export/deletion, termination, migration and correlated dependency cases.

Reviewed hospital diagnostic analysis and national emergency-response systems with clinical/public-safety, accessibility, multilingual, legal, privacy, security, reliability, provider, regulator, affected-community and independent assurance roles.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Clinical and emergency operational acceptance remain named human-review obligations outside automated validation.

evidence: Checked five-characteristic evidence precedes a cloud claim.
Checked service and deployment axes remain separate throughout classification and examples.
Checked private/public refer to eligible provisioning community rather than physical location or data visibility.
Checked hybrid claims name constituents and portability binding, while multi-cloud claims name motive and integration.
Checked managed layers retain consumer/provider/domain duties somewhere rather than deleting responsibility.
Checked exact contract and workload requirements govern security, availability, compliance, cost, portability and exit claims.
invariant_checking.notes: Offering-specific invariants require current contract, configuration, operational and provider evidence.

evidence: Reviewed counterexample showing on-premises virtualization can lack self-service, pooling, elasticity and measurement and therefore not establish private cloud.
Reviewed counterexample showing use of two public providers does not entail hybrid binding, workload portability or resilience.
Reviewed public-cloud/public-data distinction by separate provisioning-community and access-control concepts.
Reviewed service-model shorthand against managed database, Kubernetes and function ambiguity.
Confirmed executable taxonomy arithmetic and standards classification are not presented as proof of a real service or production fitness.
proof_review.notes: Arguments establish distinctions and falsifying cases, not formal verification of a cloud system.

evidence: Audited uses of cloud, essential, public, private, hybrid, serverless, managed, responsibility, portable, resilient, elastic, infinite, secure, compliant, cheap and proof.
All strong properties require exact contract, architecture and evidence beyond model names.
The executable limitation denies real classification, characteristic, responsibility, provider, isolation, security, reliability, elasticity, economic, legal and production claims.
No external academic, practitioner, clinical, public-safety, legal, regulatory or provider review is claimed.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: High-consequence use remains explicitly assigned to named institutional and human reviewers.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CLOUD-001/report.json
Reproduced three service models, four deployment models, 12 cross-axis combinations and illustrative consumer-layer counts 2/1/0 under the recorded Python 3 toolchain.
Confirmed exact expected stdout and empty stderr.

Confirmed the model is explicitly bounded to taxonomy arithmetic.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes only deterministic properties of the encoded teaching model.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter establishes provider-neutral cloud characteristics and orthogonal service/deployment taxonomies while reserving later modules' detailed ownership of shared responsibility, regions/zones, resource hierarchies, control/data planes, elasticity, managed-service operations, quotas, failure domains and requirement translation.

practitioner_review.notes: Production guidance covers role-relative classification, exact capability and control boundaries, tenancy, contract review, workload requirements, service levels, data, identity, security, metering, support, portability, provider evolution, termination, exit and bounded verification.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with ten examples and five exercises progressing from IaaS and non-cloud virtualization through PaaS, managed data, serverless, multi-cloud/hybrid distinctions, confidential SaaS, cross-cloud binding, high-stakes healthcare and legitimate non-cloud choices.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
